remarks: "Old detachable stay on bell, tubular stays on slide, which may be of a later date."² Examined by the author 1 Aug 2003. Tubular slide stays, moveable one telescopic. Bell section probably from a tenor, but may be a combination of parts of different instruments. Slide stays and adjacent ferrules have floral-leaf pattern. Other ferrules have plain rings: 6 on slide section, 1 at mouthpiece entry, 1 at slide section exit, 2 just below ferrules adjacent to slide stays, 2 near slide bow. Slide bow has ring with teeth; saddle has typical Nuremberg zigzag pattern. Bumper guard at slide bow. Tenon at slide section exit must be new work; slide tubes probably new as well. Solder repair at slide bow. slisec 1254.5.****reconcile with dimensions above. Slide section and bell section by different makers. Ferrules on bell section do not match those on slide section; ferrules in bell section have dragon-scale pattern. Ring at bell bow; saddle has zigzag pattern. 1 flat bell stay with eyelet, hinge, and pin. Garland has toothed upper edge. Bell stay decorated identically on both sides, with floral-leaf design and a maiden picking flowers. According to Carse, “An old reconstruction, and in some respects a fake. It is unlikely it owes anything to Michael Nagel; It embodies parts of an old trombone, the eyeletted bows are from another source—probably a trumpet. The bell-garland and the detachable stay are likely to be contemporary with the reconstruction. The sleeves are of several different dates.... The copper bell is breaking up and in need of consolidation; otherwise the condition is good.”³  Restored Peter Barton, 1987. Barton thinks that the garland and flat cross-stay are not old, but that the sleeves with fish-scale decoration and the two parallel tubes of the slide with chased docration are from the seventeenth century, but from 2 different instruments. A fragment of the lower bell section has come away. The frail copper bell section was found to be held together by an internal strip of selotape [sic].****check notes and see if this is direct quote.
